title: Building a HEC-HMS Rainfall-Runoff Model with Claude
goal: Building a Rainfall-Runoff Model using HECHMS
context: Flood Modeling is an important aspect of water resource engineering considering the increased frequency of extreme weather events. Information about the potential damage that a flood may cause is important. HECRAS 2D flood modeling gives that information in terms of flood water depth and velocity that may be caused by rainfall or river flow..
occupation: PhD Student + Hydraulics and Hydrological Engineer with

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: All the steps were performed satisfactorily, however, there were some discrepancies which can effect the workflow if the user has no prior knowledge of that.

Step 4.step_name: Model run and Assessment of results
Step 4.step_action: AI agent gives steps to run the model and check the results, commenting on the reliability and usability of the output.

nodes.label: Execute first run
nodes.detail: Participant executes the first simulation run (Run 1, started 12:51:13).

nodes.label: Run aborts with ET error
nodes.detail: The run aborts immediately: ERROR 22550 reports evapotranspiration data for subbasin Sb1 contains 32,862 missing values, and WARNING 15303 confirms the run was aborted.

nodes.label: Report the errors
Diagnose ET error and recommend fix
nodes.detail: Claude diagnoses that the ET gage was created but never actually assigned to the subbasin under Specified Evapotranspiration, and recommends switching the ET computation method to "Monthly Average" as a quick fix.

nodes.label: Manually adjust the settings
Apply fix and rerun successfully
nodes.detail: Participant switches Sb1's ET method to Monthly Average and reruns; the simulation now completes successfully in about 2 seconds (started 12:52:36).

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning:
Source d3: Reports ERROR 22550 that aborted the first run.
Target d4: Diagnoses error and gives steps to link and verify its data.
Reasoning: User changes ET to Monthly Average "instead of using the method which it told me"(d5). Using their own data, the rerun succeeds (d6).

nodes.label: Share the updated output and results
Report no observed data on the graph
Check in HEC-HMS
Check results, fix discharge gage link
nodes.detail: Participant checks the Results graph and Summary Table for Sink-1, finds no observed discharge line plotted, and works to fix the "Outflow" discharge gage's link as the Observed Flow for Sink-1.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source d7: Shares the run results and asks to calibrate.
Target d8: Reports no observed data on the graph, so calibration can't start.
Reasoning: User links the Outflow gage as Observed Flow on Sink-1 (d10). Claude's next response confirms the link worked.

nodes.label: Review poor calibration summary
nodes.detail: A further rerun surfaces WARNING 40017 (observed discharge gage "Outflow" has missing data); the Calibration Summary Results for Sink-1 (01Jan2000-31Dec2004) show a very poor fit: simulated peak 192.9 m³/s vs. observed 75.8 m³/s, Nash-Sutcliffe roughly -15 to -18.7, Percent Bias around 300-325%, near-zero R², and Modified Kling-Gupta around -2.2 to -2.4.

Step 5.step_action: Recommendations on how the model can be improved by changing input parameters, iteratively applied and reassessed.

nodes.label: Ask how to improve calibration
nodes.detail: Participant shares these poor results with Claude and asks how the calibration results can be improved.

nodes.label: Recommend Curve Number change
nodes.detail: Claude reviews the poor fit and recommends, as the biggest lever, changing the SCS Curve Number for Sb1 to 45, suggesting a fix order of CN first, then checking date alignment between precipitation and discharge, then fine-tuning Lag Time and Baseflow.

nodes.label: Apply CN=45 and rerun (iteration 1)
nodes.detail: Participant sets the Curve Number to 45 and reruns the simulation (around 12:56); Nash-Sutcliffe improves somewhat but remains strongly negative.

nodes.label: Assess results, suspect date misalignment
nodes.detail: Reviewing the updated calibration summary, the simulated peak timing does not align with the observed peak date.

nodes.label: Send a screenshot of the updated results to Claude
Identify precipitation/discharge date misalignment
nodes.detail: Claude flags a possible precipitation/discharge date-alignment issue as a likely root cause separate from lag time.

nodes.label: Rerun again (iteration 2)
nodes.detail: Participant reruns the model again (around 12:59:19-20) after further adjustment and checks the updated calibration summary.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source e1: Asks how to improve the poor calibration results.
Target e2: Recommends methods (e.g. Curve Number to 45 first, checking date alignment...)
Reasoning: User applies CN 45 "step one given by Claude worked" (e3), then a second change while Claude's next response (e6) is still generating, improving Nash-Sutcliffe from -18 to -13 "by following just two steps" (e7). User follows Claude's instructions.

nodes.label: Return to Claude and read the further steps
Apply changes and rerun (iteration 3)
nodes.detail: Participant applies the recommended changes and reruns twice more (around 13:01:37 and 13:03:59-13:04:00); Nash-Sutcliffe improves from about -18.7 toward approximately -13 across these iterations.

nodes.label: Conclude model remains poorly calibrated
nodes.detail: The session ends with the model still poorly calibrated overall (persistently negative Nash-Sutcliffe), attributed to the underlying DEM/meteorological-data geographic mismatch flagged earlier and to missing/incomplete observed discharge data (WARNING 40017).

Step 1.step_name: Download DEM, discharge, precipitation, temperature, evapotranspiration and meteorological data
Step 1.step_action: AI to identify a watershed which has all required data to create a rainfall-runoff model in HEC-HMS, and guide the participant through downloading it.
Step 1.output: Link to websites for downloadable DEM and rainfall data of a particular location. Steps to download required data.
Step 1.tools: Claude, HEC-RAS, USGS, NOAA and web browser
rubrics: The websites provided were reliable for downloading the required data
The DEM and rainfall data were suitable for the model
The required data sources were properly identified
The download steps were clear and easy to follow
The instructions were enough to download the required data

ratings.output_quality_reason: The model clearly identified the website correctly but did not give clear steps for interacting with the website for downloading data.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The agent gave website link for the data

Step 2.step_name: Assess the data from another source
Step 2.output: AI agent to give detailed steps to create geometry file for HECRAS simulation which should include meshing, boundary conditions, cell refinement, infiltration, Mannings values etc
rubrics: The geometry setup steps were technically correct
The mesh and refinement settings were suitable for the model
Settings such as boundary conditions, infiltration and Manning's values were included
The model setup steps were clear and easy to follow
The instructions were enough to create the geometry for simulation

ratings.output_quality_reason: The AI gave good quality steps (brief and to the point). The AI should have clearly given the location of the outflow boundary as it had access to DEM and could analyze the location of the outflow.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The agent understood the requirement and provided workable steps.

Step 3.step_action: AI model gives comprehensive, one-step-at-a-time instructions to set up the model using the participant's own prior-project data.
Step 3.output: AI agent to give unsteady flow conditions considering the geometry settings and data available. The computational settings should be based on both the geometry and unsteady flow conditions.
rubrics: The unsteady flow settings were technically correct
The settings were suitable for the available data and geometry
All important computational settings were included
The setup steps were clear and easy to follow
The instructions were enough to run the model

ratings.output_quality_reason: The AI gave all steps correctly and to the point, but it gave extra settings which were already set as default in HECRAS.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Instructions were adequate to run the model

Step 4.step_name: Model run and Assessment of results
Step 4.step_action: AI agent gives steps to run the model and check the results, commenting on the reliability and usability of the output.
Step 4.output: AI should be able to check and analyze the results and comment on its reliability and usability.
rubrics: The model results were interpreted correctly
The flood depth, velocity and flow paths were properly assessed
The hydrographs and flood maps were adequately checked
The reliability of the model results was clearly explained
The output gave a clear conclusion about the usability of the results

ratings.output_quality_reason: The interpretation of results was good. The AI model analyzed the DEM itself and compared the results.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The AI analyzed the results correctly.

Step 5.step_action: Recommendations on how the model can be improved by changing input parameters, iteratively applied and reassessed.
Step 5.output: AI agent to give specific parameters which can improve model computational efficiency and reliability of results. The parameter can be single or multiple or combined.
rubrics: The recommended parameter changes were technically correct
The recommendations were relevant to the problems in the model
The suggestions considered model reliability and efficiency
The expected effect of the changes was clearly explained
The recommendations were practical and could be applied

ratings.output_quality_reason: The AI correctly found the problems in results and gave correct recommendations.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The AI agent gave correct recommendations that could improve the model
